135	// bindWatchFlags registers the watch flags on a command, shared so `watch` and `workspace watch` expose
136	// the identical token-frugality controls.
137	func bindWatchFlags(cmd *cobra.Command, w *watchCommandOptions) {
138		cmd.Flags().DurationVar(&w.interval, "interval", w.interval, "Poll interval between ticks")
139		cmd.Flags().DurationVar(&w.consolidateEvery, "consolidate-every", w.consolidateEvery, "Minimum interval between full consolidations (heavy refresh); the per-tick short-term delta covers freshness in between. 0 = consolidate on every change; a full short-term buffer always consolidates")
140		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&w.once, "once", false, "Run a single pass and exit (no daemon loop)")
141		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&w.distill, "distill", false, "Run distill (SPENDS TOKENS) when new sessions land — gated by --distill-every + --budget")
142		cmd.Flags().DurationVar(&w.distillEvery, "distill-every", w.distillEvery, "Minimum interval between gated agent runs (distill and/or seed synthesis)")
143		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&w.distillAgent, "agent", w.distillAgent, "Agent for the distill step (used only with --distill)")
144		cmd.Flags().IntVar(&w.distillJobs, "jobs", w.distillJobs, "Parallel distill extraction jobs when --distill is enabled; reconciliation and writes remain deterministic")
145		cmd.Flags().IntVar(&w.distillMaxSessions, "max-sessions", w.distillMaxSessions, "Cap how many not-yet-distilled sessions ONE gated distill pass processes (0 = no cap). --distill-every bounds how often the daemon spends; this bounds how much each spend costs")
146		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&w.seedAgent, "seed-agent", w.seedAgent, "Agent for gated seed synthesis (SPENDS TOKENS); none = deterministic seed only. Bounded by --distill-every + --budget, NOT per-change")
147		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&w.model, "model", "", "Fast/cheap model for the gated agent steps (distill/seed)")
148		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&w.effort, "effort", "", "Reasoning effort for the gated agent steps (codex --config model_reasoning_effort=, claude --effort)")
149		cmd.Flags().IntVar(&w.budget, "budget", 0, "Cap on gated agent runs for the LIFE OF THIS PROCESS (distill + seed); 0 = unlimited. It never resets, so on a long-lived daemon --budget 1 means one run EVER, not one per window — the durable per-window guard is --distill-every + the persisted cursor. Use it only for a bounded foreground run.")
150	}

154		cmd := &cobra.Command{

156			Short: "Keep the brain up to date automatically",
157			Long:  "Keep the brain fresh automatically (deterministic refresh is free; agent steps are gated)",
158			Args:  cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),

171	func runWatch(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, w watchCommandOptions, target string) error {
172		if w.interval <= 0 {
173			w.interval = 5 * time.Minute
174		}
175		if w.distillJobs <= 0 {
176			return fmt.Errorf("--jobs must be greater than 0")
177		}
178		now := opts.Now
179		if now == nil {
180			now = time.Now
181		}
182		repoDir, local, err := base.ResolveLocalTargetRepoDir(ctx, opts.Runner, target)
183		if err != nil {
184			return err
185		}
186		if !local {
187			return fmt.Errorf("watch requires a local repository path: %s", target)
188		}
189		storage, err := repoStoragePaths(ctx, opts.Runner, opts.Env, repoDir)
190		if err != nil {
191			return err
192		}
193		cursorPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(storage.HeadPath), "watch.json")
194		// Wire SIGINT/SIGTERM so a long-running daemon stops cleanly between ticks instead of being killed
195		// mid-refresh; this is what makes the loop's ctx-cancel paths live (the root command runs with a
196		// Background context otherwise).
197		ctx, stop := watchSignalContext(ctx)
198		defer stop()
199		// Every line this daemon writes carries when, which process and build,
200		// which tick and which repo (see watchLogFields). The banner is written
201		// before the first tick, so it carries no tick number; watchLoop stamps
202		// everything from there on, and the two writers never nest.
203		banner := newWatchLogPrefixWriter(cmd.OutOrStdout(), watchLogFields{build: opts.Version, repo: storage.Key}, now)
204		fmt.Fprintf(banner, "[watch] %s — interval %s, distill=%v (every %s, agent=%s, jobs=%d, model=%q, max-sessions=%s, run-budget=%s)\n",
205			storage.Key, w.interval, w.distill, w.distillEvery, w.distillAgent, w.distillJobs, w.model,
206			watchCapLabel(w.distillMaxSessions), watchCapLabel(w.budget))
207		return watchLoop(ctx, cmd.OutOrStdout(), watchLogFields{build: opts.Version, repo: storage.Key}, now, w, cursorPath,
208			func(sink io.Writer) watchSteps {
209				return watchStepsForRepo(watchStepCommand(cmd, sink), opts, w, repoDir, now)
210			})
211	}

213	// watchCapLabel renders a cap where a non-positive value means "no cap".
214	//
215	// The banner printed a bare "budget=0", and 0 is the value a setup-installed
216	// watcher ALWAYS has: setup deliberately never passes --budget, because that
217	// counter is process-lifetime and never resets (see brainWatchDaemonArgs). So
218	// the one number the daemon's log offered about spend was both meaningless and
219	// easy to read as "zero allowed", while the cap that actually binds it --
220	// --max-sessions, carried per workspace in the machine watch plan -- was not
221	// printed at all.
222	func watchCapLabel(value int) string {
223		if value <= 0 {
224			return "uncapped"
225		}
226		return strconv.Itoa(value)
227	}

229	// watchSignalContext returns a context cancelled on SIGINT/SIGTERM so `watch` and `workspace watch`
230	// shut down cleanly between ticks (finish the current tick, then return) rather than dying abruptly.
231	func watchSignalContext(ctx context.Context) (context.Context, context.CancelFunc) {
232		return signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
233	}

235	// watchLoop drives the single-repo daemon. It owns the attribution of every
236	// line its ticks write -- stamped once per line by watchLogPrefixWriter -- so
237	// a tick cannot forget it and a line added later inherits it. The steps are
238	// built FROM the attributed sink rather than passed in already built, so the
239	// refresh/seed/distill progress lines land in the same stream, carrying the
240	// same tick and repo, instead of going unattributed to the raw stdout.
241	//
242	// out must be the RAW sink: wrapping it again outside would stamp every line
243	// twice.
244	func watchLoop(ctx context.Context, out io.Writer, fields watchLogFields, now func() time.Time, w watchCommandOptions, cursorPath string, stepsFor func(io.Writer) watchSteps) error {
245		tick := 0
246		fields.tick = &tick
247		out = newWatchLogPrefixWriter(out, fields, now)
248		steps := stepsFor(out)
249		agentCalls := 0
250		for {
251			tick++
252			if ctx.Err() != nil {
253				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] stopping")
254				return nil
255			}
256			watchTick(ctx, out, w, cursorPath, steps, &agentCalls)
257			if w.once {
258				return nil
259			}
260			select {
261			case <-ctx.Done():
262				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] stopping")
263				return nil
264			case <-time.After(w.interval):
265			}
266		}
267	}
268	
269	// watchTick runs one pass: cheap change detection, then (only on change) the free deterministic refresh,
270	// then the GATED token-spending work (seed synthesis and/or distill). agentCalls is shared across
271	// ticks/members so --budget caps total token spend across the whole run.
272	func watchTick(ctx context.Context, out io.Writer, w watchCommandOptions, cursorPath string, steps watchSteps, agentCalls *int) {
273		if steps.paused != nil && steps.paused() {
274			fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] paused — `entire-brain start` resumes")
275			return
276		}
277		// Short-term memory first, every tick: cheap (change detection + only
278		// changed transcripts), and it must never block or fail the tick; a delta
279		// failure just means the long-term path repairs freshness later.
280		bufferFull := false
281		// No delta step configured means there is no short-term path that could
282		// have failed, so the throttle applies at its normal cadence rather than
283		// treating every tick as a repair.
284		deltaHealthy := true
285		deltaNeedsReconcile := false
286		if steps.delta != nil {
287			stats, err := steps.delta(ctx)
288			if err != nil {
289				deltaHealthy = false
290				deltaNeedsReconcile = true
291				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] short-term memory update failed (continuing): %v\n", err)
292			} else {
293				// A delta that failed to scan any transcript did NOT fully carry
294				// the new work, so it must not defer consolidation.
295				deltaHealthy = stats.Failed == 0
296				bufferFull = stats.Truncated
297				deltaNeedsReconcile = stats.Files > 0 || stats.Failed > 0 || stats.Truncated
298				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] short-term memory updated (%d records from %d changed transcripts)\n", stats.Records, stats.Files)
299				if stats.Failed > 0 {
300					fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] short-term memory incomplete: %d transcripts failed to scan; consolidation will repair\n", stats.Failed)
301				}
302			}
303		}
304		// Delta state is itself a source-change signal. Do this before the git
305		// fingerprint gate so a changed/failed/overflowed export is never stranded
306		// in the short-term overlay waiting for an unrelated commit or restart.
307		if deltaNeedsReconcile && steps.reconcile != nil {
308			if err := steps.reconcile(ctx); err != nil {
309				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] memory reconciliation failed (durable overlay retained): %v\n", err)
310			} else {
311				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] long-term memory reconciliation queued")
312			}
313		}
314		cursor := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
315		// The hosted step pulls teammates' facts as much as it publishes local
316		// ones, so it must run on idle (no-change) ticks too — a machine that only
317		// receives would otherwise never sync. The defer below makes it run on
318		// every exit path from here down, including a failed refresh: a failed
319		// refresh never advances the main cursor, so a machine whose refresh
320		// always fails (e.g. the graph plugin is missing) takes that path on every
321		// tick and would otherwise be starved of the team's facts forever
322		// (COR-2114; a hand-placed call per return had already missed a path
323		// twice). It is token-free and throttled by its own cursor timestamp,
324		// advanced regardless of outcome so a failing hosted endpoint cannot turn
325		// every tick into an egress attempt. The success path still calls it
326		// explicitly BEFORE the agent steps — the `ran` guard makes the deferred
327		// call a no-op then — so the sync never inherits a context cancelled
328		// during a long agent step and burns its throttle window on an attempt
329		// that never happened.
330		factsSyncRan := false
331		runFactsSync := func() {
332			if factsSyncRan {
333				return
334			}
335			factsSyncRan = true
336			now := steps.now().UTC()
337			if steps.factsSync == nil || now.Sub(cursor.LastFactsSyncAt) < hostedSyncMinInterval {
338				return
339			}
340			attempted, err := steps.factsSync(ctx)
341			switch {
342			case err != nil:
343				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] hosted fact sync failed (local brain unaffected): %v\n", err)
344			case attempted:
345				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] hosted fact sync ran")
346			}
347			markFactsSyncAttempt(cursorPath, now)
348		}
349		defer runFactsSync()
350		fp := steps.fingerprint(ctx)
351		changed := fp != cursor.LastFingerprint || cursor.LastRefreshAt.IsZero()
352		if !changed && !(cursor.PendingSeed && w.seedAgent != "none" || cursor.PendingDistill && w.distill) {
353			fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] no change; nothing to do")
354			return
355		}
356		// Consolidation throttle: the fingerprint includes checkpoint refs, so an
357		// active agent session flips it every turn; without a throttle the heavy
358		// full refresh would run every tick exactly when the machine is busiest.
359		// A failed delta means nothing carried the new work, so the full refresh is
360		// the repair path and must not wait the whole interval (Bugbot PR #78),
361		// but it is throttled too, just on a shorter clock. The delta and the full
362		// refresh contend for the SAME brain write lock, so an unthrottled repair
363		// would fire the heavy path every tick for as long as the delta keeps
364		// failing, contending for the very lock that broke it. watchRepairWait
365		// escalates after one tick and then backs off to the normal cadence. An
366		// overflowed buffer still forces consolidation immediately: recall
367		// completeness is at risk, and a successful consolidation clears the
368		// overlay, so it cannot repeat the way a failing delta can. The first ever
369		// refresh always runs.
370		if changed && w.consolidateEvery > 0 && !cursor.LastRefreshAt.IsZero() && !bufferFull {
371			wait := w.consolidateEvery
372			state := "short-term memory is current"
373			if !deltaHealthy {
374				wait = watchRepairWait(w, cursor.ConsolidationRepairs)
375				state = fmt.Sprintf("short-term memory failed; repair refresh backing off after %d consecutive repairs", cursor.ConsolidationRepairs)
376			}
377			if since := steps.now().UTC().Sub(cursor.LastRefreshAt); since < wait {
378				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] consolidation deferred (%s since last full refresh; due in %s; %s)\n",
379					since.Round(time.Second), (wait - since).Round(time.Second), state)
380				return
381			}
382		}
383		if changed {
384			if err := steps.refresh(ctx); err != nil {
385				// A refusal to index an uncommitted worktree is not a failure: it
386				// is the expected answer while someone is working, and it recurs
387				// every tick until they commit. Treating it as a failure aborted
388				// the tick and left the cursor where it was, so the watcher made no
389				// progress at all for the whole time the tree stayed dirty
390				// (issue #327). Everything else still aborts, because an
391				// unrefreshed brain must not have tokens spent against it.
392				if strings.Contains(err.Error(), dirtyWorktreeErrorCode+":") {
393					fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] code index skipped (uncommitted worktree); continuing\n")
394				} else {
395					fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] refresh failed (skipping agent work this tick): %v\n", err)
396					return
397				}
398			}
399		}
400		runFactsSync()
401		reserved, reason, err := reserveWatchAgentSpend(cursorPath, fp, w, agentCalls, steps.now().UTC(), !deltaHealthy)
402		if err != nil {
403			fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] cursor update failed (skipping agent work this tick): %v\n", err)
404			return
405		}
406		if changed {
407			fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] refreshed (deterministic, no agent tokens)")
408		}
409	
410		if !w.agentWorkEnabled() {
411			return
412		}
413		if !reserved {
414			fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] agent work skipped: %s\n", reason)
415			return
416		}
417		// Gated token-spending work: agent seed synthesis and/or distill, at most once per --distill-every,
418		// counted against --budget. A transient failure of one step is intentionally best-effort: we still
419		// advance the spend cursor + budget below so a failed step retries on the NEXT interval, not every
420		// tick (and a step that already burned tokens before failing can't be re-run for free).
421		pending := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
422		seedDone, distillDone := false, false
423		seedAttempted := false
424		if w.seedAgent != "none" && pending.PendingSeed {
425			seedAttempted = true
426			if err := steps.seed(ctx); err != nil {
427				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] seed synthesis failed: %v\n", err)
428			} else {
429				seedDone = true
430				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] synthesized seed (agent step; spent tokens)")
431			}
432		}
433		if w.distill && pending.PendingDistill {
434			switch err := steps.distill(ctx); {
435			case errors.Is(err, errDistillPassBusy):
436				// When distill was the only agent step, nothing was spent, so nothing
437				// may be charged. Hand the window
438				// back instead of logging "spent tokens" and going quiet until the
439				// next one — otherwise a watcher installed beside `setup`'s
440				// hours-long backfill loses its first window (and, if the backfill
441				// outlives it, every window) to a pass that never ran.
442				// A seed step attempted immediately before this may already have spent
443				// tokens even when it returned an error, so its reservation must stay.
444				if seedAttempted {
445					fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] distill skipped: another pass holds this brain; the spend window remains consumed by seed synthesis")
446				} else {
447					releaseWatchAgentSpend(cursorPath, cursor.LastAgentSpendAt, agentCalls)
448					fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] distill skipped: another pass holds this brain; the spend window was NOT consumed")
449				}
450			case errors.Is(err, errDistillDeferred):
451				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] distilled capped batch; remaining sessions pending for the next spend window")
452			case err != nil:
453				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] distill failed: %v\n", err)
454			default:
455				distillDone = true
456				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] distilled facts (agent step; spent tokens)")
457			}
458		}
459		if err := withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath, func() error {
460			current := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
461			// A newer refresh owns its own pending work.
462			if current.LastFingerprint != pending.LastFingerprint || !current.LastRefreshAt.Equal(pending.LastRefreshAt) {
463				return nil
464			}
465			if seedDone {
466				current.PendingSeed = false
467			}
468			if distillDone {
469				current.PendingDistill = false
470			}
471			return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, current)
472		}); err != nil {
473			fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] completion cursor update failed: %v\n", err)
474		}
475	}
476	
477	// releaseWatchAgentSpend gives back a window reserved by reserveWatchAgentSpend
478	// when the gated step turned out to do nothing at all. previous is the
479	// LastAgentSpendAt read at the top of this tick, so the cursor lands exactly
480	// where it was; the budget counter is decremented for the same reason. Failures
481	// are deliberately silent: the worst case is the pre-existing behaviour (a
482	// window charged for a no-op), and a watcher must never die on cursor
483	// bookkeeping.
484	func releaseWatchAgentSpend(cursorPath string, previous time.Time, agentCalls *int) {
485		_ = withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath, func() error {
486			cursor := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
487			cursor.LastAgentSpendAt = previous
488			if *agentCalls > 0 {
489				*agentCalls--
490			}
491			return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
492		})
493	}
494	
495	// agentWorkEnabled reports whether any token-spending step is turned on.
496	func (w watchCommandOptions) agentWorkEnabled() bool {
497		return w.distill || w.seedAgent != "none"
498	}
499	
500	// watchStepsForRepo builds the per-repo side effects the watch loop drives. refresh is ALWAYS the free
501	// (seed-agent none) deterministic refresh; seed and distill are the gated token steps. Shared by the
502	// single-repo `watch` and the workspace fan-out so both stay token-frugal the same way.
503	// watchStepCommand hands the refresh/seed/distill steps the daemon's own
504	// attributed log sink. Those steps take a *cobra.Command only to find their
505	// output (they write progress through cmd.OutOrStdout and warnings through
506	// cmd.ErrOrStderr), and on the daemon path both belong in watch.log with the
507	// same stamp as the tick lines around them -- the `refresh: seed baseline
508	// failed` line is the exact line COR-2176 was filed about. Stderr and stdout
509	// are the same sink here because a supervised daemon's two streams are
510	// already redirected to the one file.
511	func watchStepCommand(parent *cobra.Command, sink io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
512		sub := &cobra.Command{}
513		sub.SetOut(sink)
514		sub.SetErr(sink)
515		if parent != nil {
516			if ctx := parent.Context(); ctx != nil {
517				sub.SetContext(ctx)
518			}
519		}
520		return sub
521	}
522	
523	func watchStepsForRepo(cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, w watchCommandOptions, repoDir string, now func() time.Time) watchSteps {
524		return watchSteps{
525			now:         now,
526			fingerprint: func(c context.Context) string { return watchFingerprint(c, opts.Runner, repoDir) },
527			delta:       func(c context.Context) (shortTermStats, error) { return watchShortTermDelta(c, cmd, opts, repoDir) },
528			reconcile: func(c context.Context) error {
529				_, warning, err := reconcileMemoryAndLaunch(c, opts, repoDir, "watch")
530				if warning != "" {
531					fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "warning: memory coordinator: %s\n", warning)
532				}
533				return err
534			},
535			// The daemon's own tick is unattended: nobody watches its stderr, so it
536			// must not run the destructive transcript sweep.
537			refresh: func(c context.Context) error { return watchDeterministicRefresh(c, cmd, opts, repoDir, true) },
538			seed:    func(c context.Context) error { return watchSeed(c, cmd, opts, w, repoDir) },
539			distill: func(c context.Context) error { return watchDistill(c, cmd, opts, w, repoDir) },
540			factsSync: func(c context.Context) (bool, error) {
541				storage, err := repoStoragePaths(c, opts.Runner, opts.Env, repoDir)
542				if err != nil {
543					return false, err
544				}
545				branch := hostedSyncBranch(c, opts.Runner, repoDir)
546				outcome, err := hostedFactsSyncAndPull(c, cmd.ErrOrStderr(), opts, repoDir, storage, branch)
547				if err != nil {
548					return outcome.Attempted, err
549				}
550				if branch != distillDefaultBranch {
551					also, err := hostedFactsSyncAndPull(c, cmd.ErrOrStderr(), opts, repoDir, storage, distillDefaultBranch)
552					return outcome.Attempted || also.Attempted, err
553				}
554				return outcome.Attempted, nil
555			},
556			paused: func() bool { return base.BackgroundPaused(opts.Env) },
557		}
558	}
559	
560	// markFactsSyncAttempt persists the hosted-sync throttle timestamp. Failures
561	// are silent for the same reason as releaseWatchAgentSpend: a watcher must
562	// never die on cursor bookkeeping.
563	func markFactsSyncAttempt(cursorPath string, now time.Time) {
564		_ = withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath, func() error {
565			cursor := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
566			cursor.LastFactsSyncAt = now
567			return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
568		})
569	}
570	
571	// watchShortTermDelta runs the short-term memory path for one repo: quiet
572	// (output discarded; the tick logs one summary line), deterministic, and
573	// token-free. The returned stats let the tick escalate to consolidation when
574	// the buffer overflows.
575	//
576	// The watcher runs unattended as a launchd daemon, exactly like the memory
577	// worker prepass: nobody is watching its (discarded) stderr, so it must never
578	// run the destructive transcript cache sweep. Only user-invoked export/refresh
579	// sweeps.
580	func watchShortTermDelta(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, repoDir string) (shortTermStats, error) {
581		perRepo := opts
582		perRepo.Env.RepoRoot = repoDir
583		deltaCmd := &cobra.Command{Use: "delta"}
584		deltaCmd.SetOut(io.Discard)
585		deltaCmd.SetErr(io.Discard)
586		deltaCmd.SetContext(ctx)
587		return runRefreshDeltaStats(deltaCmd, perRepo, true, true)
588	}
589	
590	// watchShouldSpend decides whether the token-spending agent work (seed and/or distill) runs this tick:
591	// only when at least one is enabled AND --distill-every has elapsed since the last agent spend
592	// (cursor-tracked across restarts) AND the --budget cap is not yet reached. This is the structural
593	// token-frugality guarantee — it bounds seed synthesis exactly like distill.
594	func watchShouldSpend(w watchCommandOptions, cursor watchCursor, agentCalls int, now time.Time) (bool, string) {
595		if !w.agentWorkEnabled() {
596			return false, "no agent steps enabled"
597		}
598		if !(cursor.LastAgentSpendAt.IsZero() || now.Sub(cursor.LastAgentSpendAt) >= w.distillEvery) {
599			return false, "--distill-every not elapsed"
600		}
601		if w.budget > 0 && agentCalls >= w.budget {
602			return false, fmt.Sprintf("--budget %d reached", w.budget)
603		}
604		return true, ""
605	}
606	
607	// watchRepairWait is the minimum time between full consolidations while the
608	// short-term delta is failing. It starts at one tick (a transient delta failure
609	// repairs on the very next pass) and doubles per consecutive repair up to the
610	// normal --consolidate-every, so a persistently failing delta degrades to the
611	// ordinary consolidation cadence instead of thrashing the shared brain write
612	// lock on every tick.
613	func watchRepairWait(w watchCommandOptions, repairs int) time.Duration {
614		wait := w.interval
615		if wait <= 0 {
616			wait = time.Minute
617		}
618		if repairs > watchRepairBackoffMax {
619			repairs = watchRepairBackoffMax
620		}
621		for i := 0; i < repairs && wait < w.consolidateEvery; i++ {
622			wait *= 2
623		}
624		if wait > w.consolidateEvery {
625			wait = w.consolidateEvery
626		}
627		return wait
628	}
629	
630	// reserveWatchAgentSpend advances the refresh cursor after a successful full
631	// refresh and decides whether the gated token work may run. repair reports
632	// whether THIS refresh ran early because the short-term delta failed; it drives
633	// the watchRepairWait backoff and is cleared by the first healthy delta.
634	func reserveWatchAgentSpend(cursorPath, fingerprint string, w watchCommandOptions, agentCalls *int, now time.Time, repair bool) (bool, string, error) {
635		var cursor watchCursor
636		var reserved bool
637		var reason string
638		err := withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath, func() error {
639			cursor = loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
640			changed := fingerprint != cursor.LastFingerprint || cursor.LastRefreshAt.IsZero()
641			if changed {
642				cursor.PendingSeed = cursor.PendingSeed || w.seedAgent != "none"
643				cursor.PendingDistill = cursor.PendingDistill || w.distill
644				cursor.LastFingerprint = fingerprint
645				cursor.LastRefreshAt = now
646				if repair {
647					if cursor.ConsolidationRepairs < watchRepairBackoffMax {
648						cursor.ConsolidationRepairs++
649					}
650				} else {
651					cursor.ConsolidationRepairs = 0
652				}
653			}
654			if !w.agentWorkEnabled() {
655				if changed {
656					return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
657				}
658				return nil
659			}
660			ok, skipReason := watchShouldSpend(w, cursor, *agentCalls, now)
661			if !ok {
662				reason = skipReason
663				if changed {
664					return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
665				}
666				return nil
667			}
668			cursor.LastAgentSpendAt = now
669			*agentCalls++
670			reserved = true
671			return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
672		})
673		return reserved, reason, err
674	}
675	
676	func withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath string, fn func() error) error {
677		root := filepath.Dir(cursorPath)
678		if info, err := os.Lstat(root); err == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
679			return fmt.Errorf("watch cursor directory must not be a symlink: %s", root)
680		} else if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
681			return err
682		}
683		if err := base.RejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents(root, brainstore.BrainLockDirName); err != nil {
684			return err
685		}
686		lock, err := brainstore.AcquireFileLock(filepath.Join(root, brainstore.BrainLockDirName, watchCursorLockName), "watch_locked", brainstore.BrainWriteLockTimeout)
687		if err != nil {
688			return err
689		}
690		defer func() { _ = lock.Close() }()
691		return fn()
692	}
693	
694	// watchFingerprint is a token-free change signal: the local checkpoint ref, the fetched (origin)
695	// checkpoint ref, and the worktree HEAD. Including the origin ref means a `git fetch` that brings in
696	// checkpoint activity from elsewhere also triggers a refresh. When all are unchanged since the cursor,
697	// there is nothing new to ingest.
698	func watchFingerprint(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, repoDir string) string {
699		rev := func(ref string) string {
700			if runner == nil {
701				return ""
702			}
703			out, _, err := runner.Run(ctx, repoDir, "git", "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref)
704			if err != nil {
705				return ""
706			}
707			return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
708		}
709		return rev(v1MainRef) + ":" + rev(v1OriginRef) + ":" + rev("HEAD")
710	}
711	
712	// watchDeterministicRefresh refreshes sessions + semantic state with the seed
713	// agent ALWAYS "none", then durably reconciles long-term conversation work.
714	// The coordinator owns projection publication, retries, and crash recovery;
715	// watch only nudges it. Agent seed synthesis remains a separate gated step.
716	//
717	// skipTranscriptSweep is the caller's own: this function is shared by the
718	// watch daemon's unattended per-tick consolidation (skip) and
719	// `workspace refresh --full`'s user-invoked per-member refresh (sweep), so the
720	// decision cannot live inside this shared body -- see
721	// watchDeterministicRefreshComponents.
722	func watchDeterministicRefresh(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, repoDir string, skipTranscriptSweep bool) error {
723		return watchDeterministicRefreshComponents(ctx, cmd, opts, repoDir, watchTickBuildsHistoryProjection, false, nil, skipTranscriptSweep)
724	}
725	
726	// watchDeterministicRefreshComponents runs the free refresh with explicit failure
727	// policy and an optional outcome observer. Setup chooses best effort; ticks fail fast.
728	//
729	// historyIndex separates the two callers that were previously identical. A
730	// watch TICK passes false: it runs every few minutes, the per-tick delta
731	// already makes new conversations recallable, and the coordinator consolidates
732	// the durable projection on its own schedule. `setup` passes true, because it
733	// is a one-shot onboarding build (the same shape as a manual `refresh`, which
734	// has always defaulted history on) and it ends by telling the user to run
735	// `entire-brain brief`. With history unbuilt that brief silently drops its
736	// transcript half and prints "history index missing" instead — setup's own
737	// recommended next command, answering with a warning about setup's own output.
738	// watchDeterministicRefreshOptions is the free path's refresh configuration,
739	// built here rather than inline so both callers' intent — above all whether the
740	// history projection is built — is readable and testable in one place.
741	func watchDeterministicRefreshOptions(historyIndex bool) refreshCommandOptions {
742		return refreshCommandOptions{
743			outputDir:       defaultExportDir,
744			checkpointLimit: defaultCheckpointLimit,
745			entireBinary:    "entire",
746			graphBinary:     "entire",
747			scope:           exportScopeAll,
748			// A tick must not bypass the durable work ledger: the per-tick delta
749			// already makes new conversations recallable while the coordinator
750			// consolidates asynchronously. A one-shot onboarding build has no next
751			// tick to wait for, so `setup` asks for it explicitly.
752			historyIndex: historyIndex,
753			semantic:     true,
754			seed: seedCommandOptions{
755				includeTests:       true,
756				maxFileBytes:       defaultSeedMaxFileBytes,
757				maxFiles:           defaultSeedMaxFiles,
758				format:             "markdown+json",
759				agent:              "none", // free: deterministic seed only; agent seed is gated via watchSeed
760				agentQuickTimeout:  2 * time.Minute,
761				agentDeepTimeout:   10 * time.Minute,
762				agentTimeoutAction: "keep-quick",
763				agentMaxInputBytes: defaultAgentMaxInput,
764			},
765		}
766	}
767	
768	// skipTranscriptSweep classifies by INVOKER, not by this function: the watch
769	// daemon's tick is unattended and passes true; `setup` and
770	// `workspace refresh --full` are user-invoked and pass false, same as
771	// `refresh`/`path --ensure`/`export`. Hardcoding a value here once silently
772	// disabled the sweep for setup.go:1925 and workspace.go's runWorkspaceRefresh
773	// too, neither of which is unattended.
774	func watchDeterministicRefreshComponents(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, repoDir string, historyIndex, bestEffort bool, component func(name string, err error), skipTranscriptSweep bool) error {
775		perRepo := opts
776		perRepo.Env.RepoRoot = repoDir
777		refreshOpts := watchDeterministicRefreshOptions(historyIndex)
778		refreshOpts.component = component
779		refreshOpts.bestEffort = bestEffort
780		refreshOpts.skipTranscriptSweep = skipTranscriptSweep
781		sub := &cobra.Command{}
782		sub.SetContext(ctx)
783		sub.SetOut(cmd.OutOrStdout())
784		sub.SetErr(cmd.ErrOrStderr())
785		if err := runRefresh(ctx, sub, perRepo, refreshOpts); err != nil {
786			return err
787		}
788		// Deterministic and token-free, like everything else in this step: index any
789		// checkpoint commits that landed since the entity index's high-water mark.
790		// Bounded and failure-silent — a missing `entire graph` provider must never
791		// fail a tick that otherwise refreshed the brain. Under a reporter it is one
792		// more degradable component, so `setup --json`, `status` and `doctor` can
793		// name it instead of losing the reason to a discarded stderr line; with no
794		// reporter the strict watch path keeps its warning and carries on exactly as
795		// before.
796		// Setup supplies the component reporter and consumes these progress lines
797		// as transient labels. Ordinary watch ticks retain their quiet behavior.
798		var entityTask, memoryTask *refreshProgressTask
799		if component != nil {
800			entityTask = newProgress(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "refresh").Begin("entity index")
801		}
802		entityErr := entities.RefreshIndexQuietly(ctx, entityConfig(perRepo), repoDir)
803		if entityTask != nil {
804			entityTask.Finish(entityErr)
805		}
806		switch {
807		case component != nil:
808			component(brainComponentEntities, entityErr)
809		case entityErr != nil:
810			fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "warning: entity index refresh skipped: %v\n", entityErr)
811		}
812		if component != nil {
813			memoryTask = newProgress(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "refresh").Begin("memory coordinator")
814		}
815		_, warning, err := reconcileMemoryAndLaunch(ctx, perRepo, repoDir, "watch")
816		if memoryTask != nil {
817			memoryTask.Finish(err)
818		}
819		if warning != "" {
820			fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "warning: memory coordinator: %s\n", warning)
821		}
822		if component != nil {
823			component(brainComponentMemory, err)
824		}
825		if bestEffort {
826			return nil
827		}
828		return err
829	}
830	
831	// watchSeed is the GATED agent seed synthesis step: it re-synthesizes the seed on the cheap --model/
832	// --effort using --seed-agent, run at most once per --distill-every and counted against --budget (see
833	// watchShouldSpend). Reuses runSeed; --update refreshes the existing seed in place.
834	func watchSeed(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, w watchCommandOptions, repoDir string) error {
835		seedOpts := seedCommandOptions{
836			update:             true,
837			includeTests:       true,
838			maxFileBytes:       defaultSeedMaxFileBytes,
839			maxFiles:           defaultSeedMaxFiles,
840			format:             "markdown+json",
841			agent:              w.seedAgent,
842			model:              w.model,
843			effort:             w.effort,
844			agentQuickTimeout:  2 * time.Minute,
845			agentDeepTimeout:   10 * time.Minute,
846			agentTimeoutAction: "keep-quick",
847			agentMaxInputBytes: defaultAgentMaxInput,
848		}
849		sub := &cobra.Command{}
850		sub.SetContext(ctx)
851		sub.SetOut(cmd.OutOrStdout())
852		sub.SetErr(cmd.ErrOrStderr())
853		return runSeed(ctx, sub, opts, seedOpts, repoDir)
854	}
855	
856	// errDistillPassBusy reports that the gated distill did NOTHING because another
857	// process already held the brain's distill pass lock. `distill` itself treats
858	// that as success — someone else is doing the work — but the watcher must not:
859	// it had already reserved the --distill-every window, so a silent success burned
860	// a whole window (24h by default) on a no-op and logged "spent tokens". `setup`
861	// creates that collision by design, spawning an hours-long detached backfill and
862	// installing a watcher that ticks immediately after.
863	var errDistillPassBusy = errors.New("another distill pass holds this brain")
864	
865	// errDistillDeferred retains pending work after a capped successful pass.
866	var errDistillDeferred = errors.New("distill has budget-deferred sessions")
867	
868	func watchDistill(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, w watchCommandOptions, repoDir string) error {
869		distillOpts := watchDistillOptions(w)
870		busy := false
871		deferred := false
872		distillOpts.onDeferredSessions = func(n int) { deferred = n > 0 }
873		distillOpts.onPassSkipped = func() { busy = true }
874		sub := &cobra.Command{}
875		sub.SetContext(ctx)
876		sub.SetOut(cmd.OutOrStdout())
877		sub.SetErr(cmd.ErrOrStderr())
878		if err := runDistill(ctx, sub, opts, distillOpts, repoDir); err != nil {
879			return err
880		}
881		if busy {
882			return errDistillPassBusy
883		}
884		if deferred {
885			return errDistillDeferred
886		}
887		return nil
888	}
889	
890	func watchDistillOptions(w watchCommandOptions) distillCommandOptions {
891		jobs := w.distillJobs
892		if jobs <= 0 {
893			jobs = 1
894		}
895		// A negative cap is a typo, not "unlimited". Only an explicit 0 means that.
896		maxSessions := w.distillMaxSessions
897		if maxSessions < 0 {
898			maxSessions = 0
899		}
900		return distillCommandOptions{
901			agent:               w.distillAgent,
902			model:               w.model,
903			effort:              w.effort,
904			timeout:             defaultDistillTimeout,
905			maxChunkBytes:       defaultDistillChunkSize,
906			confidenceThreshold: defaultFactConfidenceThreshold,
907			// The per-pass VOLUME cap. A capped pass is ordered newest-first,
908			// matching what `setup` says it did and what a reader wants first; the
909			// deferred remainder stays UNCACHED, so the next window picks it up
910			// rather than it being skipped forever. Ordering is left alone when
911			// there is no cap, so an uncapped `watch --distill` is unchanged.
912			maxSessions: maxSessions,
913			newestFirst: maxSessions > 0,
914			// concurrency is what the distill pipeline (and runDistill's guard)
915			// actually reads. Leaving it at the zero value made every gated distill
916			// the watcher ever attempted fail with "--concurrency must be greater
917			// than 0" before making a single agent call. There used to be a second
918			// `jobs` field to keep in step with it; `--jobs` is now a spelling of
919			// --concurrency rather than a field, so there is only one value to set.
920			concurrency: jobs,
921		}
922	}
923	
924	func loadWatchCursor(path string) watchCursor {
925		var c watchCursor
926		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
927		if err != nil {
928			return c
929		}
930		_ = json.Unmarshal(data, &c)
931		return c
932	}
933	
934	func saveWatchCursor(path string, c watchCursor) error {
935		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o700); err != nil {
936			return err
937		}
938		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(c, "", "  ")
939		if err != nil {
940			return err
941		}
942		return brainstore.WriteFileAtomic(path, append(data, '\n'), 0o600)
943	}

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"os"
9		"runtime"
10	
11		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/command/daemonreregister"
12	)
13	
14	// errWatchBinaryReplaced ends the supervised loop when the executable this
15	// daemon was started from has been replaced on disk. A long-running daemon
16	// otherwise outlives its binary: after an upgrade it keeps running the old
17	// build, whose writer-path manifest load correctly refuses the new build's
18	// fields, and every tick fails forever while `status` still says running
19	// (COR-2174). Exiting hands the restart to the service manager, which spawns
20	// the current binary.
21	var errWatchBinaryReplaced = errors.New("binary replaced on disk")
22	
23	// watchBinaryChanged returns a probe reporting whether this process's
24	// executable has been replaced since the probe was created, or nil when the
25	// executable cannot be resolved (then the staleness check is simply off).
26	func watchBinaryChanged() func() bool {
27		path, err := os.Executable()
28		if err != nil {
29			return nil
30		}
31		return watchBinaryChangeProbe(path)
32	}
33	
34	func watchBinaryChangeProbe(path string) func() bool {
35		started, err := os.Stat(path)
36		if err != nil {
37			return nil
38		}
39		return func() bool {
40			current, err := os.Stat(path)
41			if err != nil {
42				// Mid-replace or unreadable: decide on a later pass rather than
43				// restarting onto a binary that may be half-written.
44				return false
45			}
46			// All three signals carry weight: SameFile catches install-by-rename,
47			// ModTime catches the in-place rebuild, Size catches an in-place copy
48			// that preserved mtime (cp -p, rsync -t).
49			return !os.SameFile(started, current) ||
50				!current.ModTime().Equal(started.ModTime()) ||
51				current.Size() != started.Size()
52		}
53	}
54	
55	// relaunchInstalledDaemon re-registers the launchd agent after the supervised
56	// daemon exits over a replaced binary.
57	//
58	// Exiting is not enough on darwin: launchd records the cdhash of an
59	// ad-hoc-signed service binary at registration, so after the binary is rebuilt
60	// every KeepAlive respawn fails with OS_REASON_CODESIGNING ("needs LWCR
61	// update") until the agent is re-registered (COR-2174). The re-registration
62	// has to run from a detached child because bootout kills this very process —
63	// and the child is the replaced binary itself running `daemon-reregister`, so
64	// the verbs, the registration lock, and the unit rendering all stay in
65	// installDaemon rather than being restated in a shell string. The child's
66	// output goes to the daemon log, so a failed bootstrap is diagnosable there.
67	//
68	// On linux a plain exit suffices — systemd's Restart=always relaunches the
69	// current binary with no signing pin — so everything but darwin is a no-op.
70	// Failures only cost the self-restart: the daemon still exits, launchd still
71	// attempts a respawn, and `setup` re-registers on its next run.
72	func relaunchInstalledDaemon(out io.Writer, env EntireEnv) {
73		if runtime.GOOS != "darwin" || daemonRegistrationDisabled() {
74			return
75		}
76		binary, err := os.Executable()
77		if err != nil {
78			fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] launchd re-registration skipped: %v\n", err)
79			return
80		}
81		fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] re-registering with launchd so the restart lands on the current binary")
82		logPath, _ := daemonLogPath(env)
83		if _, err := spawnDetached(setupBackfillPlan{
84			Binary:  binary,
85			Args:    []string{"daemon-reregister"},
86			LogPath: logPath,
87		}); err != nil {
88			fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] launchd re-registration failed (re-run `entire-brain setup` to restart the watcher): %v\n", err)

17	// written as bare `[watch] ...` lines carrying none of that. Diagnosing the
18	// write.lock race (COR-2175) meant correlating a "reconciliation queued" line
19	// with a "refresh failed" line further down and GUESSING they were the same
20	// tick on the same repo -- which was only possible at all because one repo
21	// dominated that machine's log. Diagnosing the upgrade wedge (COR-2174) meant
22	// inferring which binary wrote a line from process start times and binary
23	// mtimes, because the log never said.

26	// tick is nil for lines written outside a tick (the startup banner); when set
27	// it is read at write time, so one writer tracks a loop's counter as it
28	// advances rather than freezing the value it was built with.

30		pid   int
31		build string
32		tick  *int
33		repo  string
34	}

39	// line added later cannot forget it, and per line rather than per write, so a
40	// two-line write does not leave its second line unattributed.
41	type watchLogPrefixWriter struct {
42		// mu makes this writer safe for concurrent use, which is a contract rather
43		// than a repair.
44		//
45		// No goroutine writes to one of these today, and that was checked rather
46		// than assumed: the module's goroutines return everything over channels,
47		// agent subprocesses get capped buffers instead of this sink, and the only
48		// progress goroutine is gated behind a TTY check that begins by asserting
49		// the writer is an *os.File -- which this never is. So there is no live
50		// race.

53		// one instance and hands it to distill, refresh and seed as both stdout and
54		// stderr, and distill owns a --jobs worker pool. Both facts that keep that

59		// mis-attribution rather than a crash.

76		}

82		}

88	// offset that changes with the reader's zone is one more thing to reconcile.

99		}

101			b.WriteString(" repo=")
102			b.WriteString(w.fields.repo)
103		}
104		b.WriteByte(' ')
105		return b.String()
106	}
107

109		if len(p) == 0 {
110			return 0, nil
111		}
112		// Held across the sink write as well as the state update: releasing before
113		// w.out.Write would keep midLine consistent while still letting two
114		// writers' bytes interleave inside one line.
115		w.mu.Lock()
116		defer w.mu.Unlock()
117		stamp := w.prefix()
118		var buf bytes.Buffer
119		for _, line := range bytes.SplitAfter(p, []byte("\n")) {
120			// SplitAfter yields a trailing empty element for a newline-terminated
121			// input; skip it rather than emit a bare prefix.
122			if len(line) == 0 {
123				continue
124			}
125			if !w.midLine {

127			}
128			buf.Write(line)
129			w.midLine = line[len(line)-1] != '\n'
130		}
131		if _, err := w.out.Write(buf.Bytes()); err != nil {
132			return 0, err
133		}

135		// count makes io.Copy and friends treat the write as failed.
